details.description: Reverb is Rev AI's automatic speech recognition model for English audio, built by Rev (Rev.com), a speech-to-text and captioning company. It was trained on 200,000 hours of human-transcribed audio and offers a tunable verbatimicity setting that lets users choose between a clean, readable transcript and a fully verbatim one, and pairs with Rev's own Reverb Diarization models for speaker separation. Rev has open-sourced the inference and evaluation code for Reverb on GitHub, with model weights published on Hugging Face under a separate model license, and also sells a separate Reverb Foreign Language product for non-English audio.
advantages: Rev reports 9.68% WER on Earnings21, 13.68% on Earnings22, and 10.30% on Rev16, ahead of Whisper Large-v3 (14.26%, 19.05%, 10.86%) and Canary-1B (14.40%, 19.01%, 13.82%) on the same test sets.
Trained on 200,000 hours of human-transcribed audio.
Offers a tunable verbatimicity parameter to control how verbatim versus clean the output transcript is, suited to both readable transcripts and audio-editing workflows.
Pairs with Rev's Reverb Diarization V2 model, which reports 0.046 WDER on Earnings21 and 0.078 on Rev16, improving on Pyannote 3.0's 0.051 and 0.090.
Inference and evaluation code are open-sourced on GitHub, with model weights available on Hugging Face.
disadvantages: Limited to English audio; non-English transcription requires Rev AI's separate Reverb Foreign Language model.
use_cases: Clean, readable transcription of long-form English audio.
Audio-editing workflows that need verbatim transcripts with precise word-level timing.
Multi-speaker transcription combined with Reverb Diarization for speaker separation.

sources.title: revdotcom/reverb: Reverb - Open source inference and evaluation code for Rev's state-of-the-art speech recognition and diarization models

notes: The GitHub README and Hugging Face card describe only the English 'reverb-asr' (reverb_asr_v1) model; no multilingual or foreign-language variant is documented there, matching the separate 'Reverb Foreign Language' product on the pricing page. Rev's changelog shows the low-cost 'Reverb Turbo' transcriber option was deprecated 2026-07-28, but has no deprecation entry for the standard 'reverb' transcriber as of this research date. A separate Rev marketing PDF ('Rev ASR v3') advertises newer WER/diarization numbers, but never uses the name 'Reverb' and its Earnings-21 WER (7.24-7.60%) differs from the GitHub repo's published 9.68%, so it was not used here since it could not be confirmed to describe this same model.
